feedback:
Judged from earlier races and this candidate's contents only. Nothing here states how the candidate will perform.

The candidate is the iteration 8 and 9 design, unchanged: sensor span x = -0.05, -0.025, 0.0, 0.025, 0.05 with weights (-2, -1, 0, 1, 2), kd 0.6, kp 4.0, ki 0.2, base_speed 1.5, sensor_size 0.012 and last_direction. Iteration 8 and its unchanged re-run in iteration 9 both scored 323.64, so the simulator appears deterministic for this design and a further identical race adds no new information beyond locking that score.

Evidence: the span widened from 0.04 to 0.05 at kd 0.6 raised oval finishes from 12 to 14 of 20 and cut s-bend line losses from 1.00 to 0.75 (iterations 7 to 8). Slalom losses held at 1.00. Span 0.06 at kd 0.55 (iteration 5) cut losses further but cost oval finishes, so the useful span is probably between 0.04 and 0.06. Lowering kd has hurt every time it was tested (kd 0.55 at span 0.04 scored 238 against 282 at kd 0.6), so kd 0.6 stays. Speed 1.3 (iteration 2) and sensor_size 0.016 (iteration 6) both lowered the score and stay closed. Oval steering_oscillation rose to 0.40 at this span, above the 0.32 caution level, but the score is the decisive measure.

Why approve: this is the best raced design, it is already measured at 323.64, and every single-variable alternative I can justify is either untested at this span or has a record of lowering the score (kd down, speed down, sensor_size up). A revision spends two action runs and could land below 323.64. Approving locks the measured baseline.

For the last iteration after this one, the best use of the next design is a span test between the measured points, not a kd change. Read the next race as follows. If the score holds near 323, keep the span at 0.05 and kd at 0.6. Treat the remaining s-bend and slalom losses as limits of the sensing layout, not a damping issue.
requested_changes: Next iteration, test sensor span x = -0.045, -0.0225, 0.0, 0.0225, 0.045 at kd 0.6 with weights unchanged. Span 0.04 scored 282.45 and span 0.05 scored 323.64, while span 0.06 cut losses but cost oval finishes (iteration 5), so an in-between span is the untested point.

If that span scores below 323.64 or oval finishes drop below 14 of 20, keep the iteration 8 span of 0.05 at kd 0.6 as the final design. Do not raise kd above 0.6, since kd 0.55 scored below kd 0.6 at span 0.04.

Hold kp 4.0, ki 0.2, base_speed 1.5, sensor_size 0.012 and last_direction fixed. Iteration 2 (speed 1.3, score 86.8) and iteration 6 (sensor_size 0.016, score 157.9) both lowered the score, so these stay fixed to keep effects separable.
